skill.name: migrating-to-db
skill.description: Expert guidance for migrating Logseq graphs from Markdown (MD) format to the new Database (DB) format. Auto-invokes when users ask about MD to DB migration, converting graphs, import options, data transformation, or compatibility between Logseq versions. Covers migration strategies, common issues, and best practices.
skill.summary: Plan, execute, and validate a Logseq Markdown-to-DB graph migration.

content.value_statement: Logseq graph migrations can lose structure, types, links, and query behavior. This skill provides a staged plan for backup, import decisions, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Compares Markdown and database graph behavior for storage, tags, properties, queries, and synchronization.
Creates a pre-migration checklist covering backups, namespaces, tags, properties, templates, and links.
Guides EDN export, database graph creation, import configuration, and post-migration review.
Explains tag-to-class conversion, namespace handling, and property type choices.
Provides validation query examples and troubleshooting guidance for common migration issues.
limitations: Does not execute migrations, import files, or modify Logseq graphs.
Describes the 2024-2025 alpha state, so current Logseq behavior may differ.
Does not guarantee compatibility with every plugin, query, template, or synchronization workflow.
Validation query examples may require changes for the installed Logseq version and graph schema.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Personal Graph
use_cases.description: Create a backup, inventory graph features, and choose migration settings before importing a personal knowledge base.

use_cases.title: Protect a Team Workspace
use_cases.description: Plan a parallel migration with validation checkpoints for shared content, queries, and collaboration workflows.

use_cases.title: Adapt Logseq Integrations
use_cases.description: Map changed attributes and review compatibility risks before updating queries, plugins, or automated workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a beginner checklist for migrating my small Logseq Markdown graph to DB. Include backup, export, import, and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first-time user needs a clear migration sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Review Graph Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me audit my graph before migration. I use [tags], [namespaces], [properties], [templates], and [queries]. Identify decisions and risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs guidance tailored to existing graph features.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Parallel Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parallel migration plan for a large active graph. Define phases, rollback points, validation checks, and criteria for switching to DB.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team must keep working while evaluating the DB graph.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Validation Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced validation strategy for my migration. Cover counts, orphaned blocks, property types, references, namespaces, and rewritten queries.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced user needs evidence that the migrated graph is complete.

output_examples.input: Plan a safe migration for my small graph with tags and date properties.
output: Create and verify a complete backup before changing the graph.
Export the graph, then test import into a separate DB graph.
Decide which tags become classes and verify inferred date types.
Compare page, block, property, and reference counts before switching.

output_examples.input: My page references broke after migration. What should I check?
output_examples.output: Compare page names before and after import, inspect namespace handling, identify renamed targets, and repair references only after confirming the intended mapping.

output_examples.input: Should our team migrate everything at once?
output_examples.output: Use a parallel migration for a large active graph. Test representative content, define rollback points, validate critical workflows, and switch only after acceptance checks pass.

best_practices: Keep the original Markdown graph unchanged until the DB graph passes validation.
Test a representative subset before importing the full graph.
Record tag, namespace, property, and query decisions before migration.
anti_patterns: Do not delete the source graph immediately after import.
Do not accept inferred property types without checking important fields.
Do not assume old queries, plugins, and templates work unchanged.

faq.question: Does this skill migrate my graph automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning, configuration, validation, and troubleshooting guidance but does not access or modify your graph.

faq.question: Which export format does the guidance recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends EDN export for full graph data before creating and importing into a separate DB graph.

faq.question: Should every tag become a class?
faq.answer: No. Review tag meaning and required properties, then convert only tags that benefit from class behavior.

faq.question: How should namespaces be handled?
faq.answer: Choose flattening or hierarchy deliberately. Review duplicate names and rename conflicting pages before migration.

faq.question: How can I verify the migration?
faq.answer: Compare counts, check orphaned blocks, inspect property types, test references, and update important queries.

faq.question: Is the guidance current for every Logseq release?
faq.answer: No. The source describes the 2024-2025 alpha period, so confirm current features and migration behavior in official documentation.
